channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: More execs face losing pay rise under ‘punitive’ rules
item.description: Executives at a “large number” of trusts and integrated care boards could lose their annual pay rise under new oversight rules, the NHS Alliance has warned.

item.title: ICB mergers suspended due to ‘devolution discussions’
item.description: Twenty clustered integrated care boards that had expected to merge next year must wait until at least 2028 while government considers the implications of the prime minister’s devolution agenda, they have been told.

item.title: High repeat surgery rates under review at five trusts
item.description: At least five trusts are reviewing their rates of repeat breast cancer surgery after recording levels significantly above the maximum expected level, HSJ has learned.

item.title: How do you solve a problem like East Kent?
item.description: In 2021, HSJ wrote 48 news stories mentioning East Kent Hospitals University Foundation Trust.

item.title: ICB faces potential legal battle over funding row
item.description: Three GP practices are threatening to sue their integrated care board over its plans to cut premises funding.

item.title: Staff exodus to private rivals forces trust to restrict service
item.description: A mental health and community trust has been forced to restrict its children’s ADHD service after a string of staff left for private providers.

item.title: ‘Organisational shame’ driving defensive behaviour at inquiry trust
item.description: Staff at a trust subject to a statutory inquiry are paralysed by fear, a review has discovered.

item.title: Hospital boss to become regional director
item.description: A hospital chief executive has been made London’s interim regional director role after NHS England concluded it would take longer than expected to make a permanent appointment.

item.title: Government alert sounded over EPR cyber security risk
item.description: The “concentration” of electronic patient record systems under a relatively small number of suppliers has increased the risk of highly damaging cyber attack, a government review has concluded.

item.title: North-south divide opens up in ambulance services
item.description: Every ambulance trust in the south of England is missing the national category 2 response target so far this year, while all three northern trusts are inside it after a more sustained recovery.

item.title: The stubborn insanity of NHS finances
item.description: “No one tells the truth about their financial position” – so a respected chief executive of a trust with an income north of £1bn informed HSJ last week.

item.title: CEO ‘shocked’ by latest maternity findings
item.description: An acting chief executive has said it was “quite shocking” to find his trust had “let so many people down” on maternity care, contrary to assurances given to the board.

item.title: Worst-rated trust gets new CEO for six months
item.description: The worst-rated acute trust in England has hired an experienced interim chief executive while its incumbent takes leave.

item.title: Revealed: NHSE plan to ‘grip’ GP performance
item.description: NHS England intends to “improve operational grip” on GP performance and has warned it may lead to “contractual action”.

item.title: ‘Data centre problem’ cancels clinics at multiple hospitals
item.description: A problem at a data centre owned by a US tech giant saw multiple hospital trusts unable to access their electronic patient record systems yesterday.

item.title: NHSE ‘bringing in staff without due process’
item.description: NHS England’s internal whistleblowing champions raised concerns that the organisation is bringing in staff “without due process”.

item.title: ‘Disjointed’ tech projects must be accelerated, says NHSE board
item.description: NHS England’s technology committee has warned that “disjointed” key national tech programmes are “falling short of our ambitions” amid a “slow pace of delivery”.

item.title: ICBs face £6m legal bill as ‘complex’ contract dispute drags on
item.description: Two thirds of integrated care boards have been caught up in a multi-million-pound legal challenge brought by a waste management firm.

item.title: CEO drafted in to lead trust out of hospital group
item.description: A new chief executive has been appointed to oversee Northern Lincolnshire and Goole Foundation Trust’s departure from its troubled group with Hull University Teaching Hospitals Trust.

item.title: Patients missing out on drugs due to NHS cost-cutting, claims minister
item.description: The NHS’s success in driving down the cost of drugs has meant fewer medicines are available for patients, a government minister has admitted.
